topic: TencentCloud AgentObs SDK for DeepSeek Harness: GenAI Trace Observability

key_points: First-party TencentCloud plugin (Apache-2.0), created 2026-08-18, latest release v0.0.1 (2026-08-18) — npm package version is 0.1.0, so the tag and package version do not match
Observes DSH native session, agent loop, LLM stream and tool lifecycle; converts to Tencent Cloud's 5-layer span model (entry -> agent -> step -> chat -> tool)
Transport is Protobuf direct to Tencent Cloud Log Service via tencentcloud-cls-sdk-js — no OTLP collector, no sidecar; the README states this as the headline feature
Two auth modes: strong auth (CLS_SECRET_ID + CLS_SECRET_KEY) or weak auth (numeric UIN only, no key)
Documented failure modes are concrete: pnpm v9+ blocks protobufjs build scripts (ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS, fix is enable-scripts=true + pnpm install), and the plugin must be restarted after install

Tunables: batchMaxSize 32, maxBatchBytes 10MB (must stay under the SDK's 19MB hard limit or the whole batch is rejected locally), maxQueueSize 2048 (drops oldest span when full), flushIntervalMs 5000, retryTimes 3, contentMaxChars 128000
Node.js >=18.0.0 — lower floor than the OpenTelemetry competitor, so older fleets are eligible
The direct competitor: community Apache-2.0 OpenTelemetry plugin, 26 stars / 4 forks / 5 open issues, latest v0.1.2 (2026-08-25) — more stars, more issues, more releases than the Tencent plugin
Produces the same trace shape (ENTRY -> AGENT -> STEP -> LLM/TOOL) but exports standard OTLP/HTTP protobuf to any backend: Jaeger, Grafana Tempo, SigNoz, Langfuse

Each real LLM attempt gets its own LLM span so retries stay visible under the same step; tool calls correlate to results by DSH call ID; errors/aborts close spans with error status instead of leaving them open
Also exports the standard gen_ai.client.operation.duration and gen_ai.client.token.usage metrics (the Tencent plugin's documented surface is traces)

Content capture is OFF by default; enabling it can send source code, credentials and personal data to the backend. It also owns private TracerProvider/MeterProvider and never replaces DSH's global provider
Compatibility: DSH >=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.2.0, Node.js >=22.19.0, fully verified on 0.1.0-rc.6 headless and Web profiles, Node 22.19/24.19/25.9 on macOS
Community MIT plugin (v0.7.0, created 2026-08-14) for the dsh-plugin topic, explicitly not part of the official repo — the highest-versioned of the DSH tracing plugins

Exports each turn as an OpenTelemetry trace (model step -> generation, tool call -> tool span), groups traces by session, records canonical feedback as Langfuse Scores, and preserves fork/subagent lineage
Implements the harness's public telemetry seam @deepseek-ai/dsh-session-telemetry as an alternative backend to the official OTLP-logs exporter
Represents the 'LLM-product-team' route: self-host or subscribe Langfuse rather than push traces into a cloud log service

The harness itself is the constraint every plugin answers to: it ships a public telemetry seam, @deepseek-ai/dsh-session-telemetry (v0.0.1-rc.1, 2026-08-10, BSD-3-Clause), which is the contract plugins implement to receive session, agent-loop, LLM-stream and tool-lifecycle events

The seam accepts exactly ONE backend per context: loading a duplicate backend (for example the official OTLP-logs exporter plus a tracing plugin, or two tracing plugins) throws an error at load time — DSH tracing plugins are mutually exclusive, not stackable
The official repo also ships an OTLP-logs exporter implementing the same seam; choosing a tracing plugin means replacing it, not adding to it

Tencent Cloud's own CLS documentation covers the DSH integration: install tencentcloud-agentobs-sdk-dsh, then read Agent Observability in the CLS console, confirming the plugin is an officially supported ingestion path rather than a community experiment

Promised console outputs: full call chain of a single task with parent-child relationships among Agents, reasoning steps, model calls and tool calls; per-step duration, TTFT, input/output/cached tokens; success status, failure reasons and retry process; multi-round task relationships within a session

The same doc set covers sibling SDKs for AgentScope (tencentcloud-agentobs-sdk-agentscope) and OpenAI Agents (tencentcloud-agentobs-sdk-openai-agent), and a Langfuse-SDK-to-CLS OTLP path — Tencent is building a family of ingestion routes into one CLS 'Agent Observability' surface
CLS console surfaces a management dashboard with Applications Connected, Applications Reporting Data, Total Data Written Yesterday and Total Tokens Yesterday
CLS is pay-as-you-go by default and the bill has multiple line items, so 'zero collector' does not mean 'zero cost' — cost simply moves from infrastructure you run to consumption you meter

Chinese mainland pay-as-you-go rates: log write traffic USD 0.032/GB/day, standard index traffic USD 0.062/GB/day, standard log storage USD 0.0024/GB/day, standard index storage USD 0.0024/GB/day, data processing USD 0.026/GB/day, partition USD 0.007/partition/day, service requests USD 0.026 per million/day

Index traffic is the most expensive line and is billed on UNCOMPRESSED volume, while write traffic and storage are billed on compressed volume (typical compression 1:4 to 1:10) — the choice to index trace fields drives the bill
Resource packs are denominated in U where 1U = CNY 1 and can offset any billable item; 'billed on raw log volume' mode exists as an alternative but is whitelist-only
Our own site already published this product on 2026-08-20: 'TencentCloud AgentObs SDK for DeepSeek Harness: Zero-Collector GenAI Trace Observability' (slug tencentcloud-agentobs-dsh-genai-traces)

That post already owns the install walkthrough (profile add + pnpm approve-builds), the 5-layer span model, the full config/preference table, the privacy and batching sections, and a 4-way comparison table

Canonical cannibalization risk for this review: restating the walkthrough would compete with a page that already ranks for the product name; the new piece must be reframed as a later, evidence-based judgement rather than a second explainer

That post's comparison already names dsh-plugin-langfuse, dsh-Agentlink, dsh-plugin-opentelemetry-tracing and the generic OTLP route, so the review's comparison must add measured adoption, privacy defaults and cost arithmetic to be additive

Our site also owns the vendor-neutral counterpoint (2026-08-16, 'OpenTelemetry Tracing for DeepSeek Harness: A Complete Setup Guide') covering the telemetry seam, one-backend-per-context restriction, and the Jaeger/Tempo/SigNoz/Langfuse backend table
Useful internal-link target and the natural 'alternative' anchor when the review argues lock-in versus portability
Together the two existing posts mean this review should be written as the third act: decision and cost, not setup

stats.fact: TencentCloud/tencentcloud-agentobs-sdk-dsh: 14 stars, 3 forks, 0 open issues, Apache-2.0, created 2026-08-18, last push 2026-08-26 (checked 2026-10-01)
Latest GitHub release is v0.0.1 (2026-08-18) while the npm package's latest version is 0.1.0 (first published 2026-08-18T03:42Z, last modified 2026-08-26) — tag and package version are inconsistent
npm downloads for tencentcloud-agentobs-sdk-dsh: 519 in the last 30 days (2026-08-31 to 2026-09-29) and 121 in the last 7 days (2026-09-23 to 2026-09-29)

The OpenTelemetry competitor @loongsuite/dsh-plugin drew 1,978 downloads in the same 30 days and 789 in the last 7 days — roughly 3.8x and 6.5x the Tencent plugin, on a repo with 26 stars / 4 forks / 5 open issues and a v0.1.2 release dated 2026-08-25

The tencentcloud-agentobs-sdk-dsh npm package has exactly two runtime dependencies (@deepseek-ai/schemastery, tencentcloud-cls-sdk-js) and requires Node.js >=18.0.0; @loongsuite/dsh-plugin requires Node.js >=22.19.0 and pulls the OpenTelemetry SDK stack

DeepSeek Harness ships a public telemetry seam, @deepseek-ai/dsh-session-telemetry (v0.0.1-rc.1, published 2026-08-10, BSD-3-Clause), described as 'session-event capture, projection, redaction, and handoff to a reporting backend'

The telemetry seam accepts exactly one backend per context: loading a duplicate backend (official OTLP-logs exporter plus a tracing plugin, or two tracing plugins) throws an error at load time — the Tencent plugin and the OpenTelemetry plugin cannot both be active in one profile

Privacy default is inverted between the two leading DSH tracing plugins: tencentcloud-agentobs-sdk-dsh ships captureContent: true (prompts, responses, tool arguments and results attached to spans by default) while @loongsuite/dsh-plugin ships content capture off by default
stats.source: github.com/TencentCloud/tencentcloud-agentobs-sdk-dsh README (隐私说明 / captureContent default true); github.com/loongsuite/dsh-plugin README (Privacy and runtime behavior)

stats.fact: Both leading plugins pin the same harness window (>=0.1.0-rc.6 and <0.2.0); both state that outside that range lifecycle hooks may not fire, so traces can silently stop appearing at the 0.2.0 boundary

Buffering behaviour of the Tencent plugin: batchMaxSize 32 spans, maxBatchBytes 10MB (must be below the CLS SDK's 19MB hard limit or the batch is rejected locally), maxQueueSize 2048 spans after which the OLDEST span is silently dropped, flushIntervalMs 5000, retryTimes 3

Tencent Cloud CLS Chinese-mainland pay-as-you-go list prices: log write traffic USD 0.032/GB/day, standard index traffic USD 0.062/GB/day, standard log storage USD 0.0024/GB/day, standard index storage USD 0.0024/GB/day, data processing USD 0.026/GB/day, partition USD 0.007/partition/day, service requests USD 0.026 per million/day; resource-pack unit 1U = CNY 1

CLS bills index traffic on uncompressed volume while write traffic and storage are billed on compressed volume (typical log compression 1:4 to 1:10), so enabling more indexed trace fields is the dominant cost lever — Tencent's own worked example shows index traffic and index storage as the two largest line items
stats.source: cloud.tencent.com/document/product/614/45802 (计费概述) and 购买指南 PDF (614_45801_cn.pdf)

stats.fact: Tencent Cloud positions CLS Agent Observability as one console across multiple ingestion routes, with official SDKs for DeepSeek Harness (tencentcloud-agentobs-sdk-dsh), AgentScope (tencentcloud-agentobs-sdk-agentscope) and OpenAI Agents (tencentcloud-agentobs-sdk-openai-agent), plus a Langfuse-SDK OTLP path and a resident local collector (LoongSuite Pilot) that auto-detects AI coding agents

CLS console reports Agents Observability management metrics including Applications Connected, Applications Reporting Data, Total Data Written Yesterday and Total Tokens Yesterday — i.e. cost and adoption are observable from the same console the traces land in

angles: CANONICAL DIFFERENTIATION (do not skip): the site already published this exact product on 2026-08-20 at slug tencentcloud-agentobs-dsh-genai-traces ('...Zero-Collector GenAI Trace Observability'), which owns the install walkthrough, 5-layer span model, config table, privacy section and a 4-way comparison. This review must be written as the third act — a source-backed judgement six weeks later — and must internally link that post instead of repeating its setup steps. If the draft re-explains installation it is cannibalizing our own ranking page.

Privacy default inversion: the Tencent plugin ships content capture ON (captureContent: true, contentMaxChars 128000) while the OpenTelemetry competitor ships it OFF. For a coding agent that reads source trees, .env files and tool output, a default-on trace payload is a compliance decision, not a checkbox — lead the review with this divergence.

Zero collector does not mean zero cost: the plugin removes infrastructure you operate but converts it into metered CLS consumption, and because index traffic is billed on uncompressed volume at roughly 2x write-traffic rates, the bill follows how many span fields you index, not how many traces you emit. Do the arithmetic on a plausible DSH workload and contrast with self-hosted Jaeger/Langfuse where marginal ingestion cost is near zero.

Adoption reality check: 14 stars and 519 monthly npm downloads for a first-party SDK whose last push was 2026-08-26, versus 1,978/30 days for the community OpenTelemetry plugin. Frame this as maturity evidence for an evaluation, not as a verdict — the Tencent plugin is also only 0.1.0.

The one-backend rule changes the decision shape: because the DSH telemetry seam accepts exactly one backend per context, you cannot run this and an OTLP tracing plugin together — the choice is made at install time per profile. Give readers the migration cost of reversing it.

Vendor lock-in tested concretely: transport is Protobuf to CLS, not OTLP, so the portability question is 'can I replay the same trace into another backend?'. Answer with the auth modes (SecretId/SecretKey vs numeric UIN), the CLS-bound field mapping, and what leaves with you.

Version-window risk is shared but asymmetric: both plugins pin >=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.2.0, yet Tencent's Node floor is 18 versus 22.19 for the OTel plugin — the Tencent plugin is easier to adopt into an older fleet and equally exposed to the 0.2.0 cliff.

Operational honesty: queue overflow silently drops the OLDEST span at 2048 buffered spans. Reframe 'dropped spans' as a monitoring signal rather than a bug, and pair it with the plugin's own documented silent-failure modes (expired CLS key returning 401 while the harness exits 0).

Positioning against the vendor family: dsh is one of several ingestion routes (AgentScope, OpenAI Agents, Langfuse OTLP, LoongSuite Pilot) into one CLS Agent Observability console. The review's real question is 'should DSH traces live in CLS at all', which is a stack decision above the plugin.

Concrete decision matrix instead of a verdict: Tencent Cloud-native teams with existing CLS topics and retention policy win; everyone else pays lock-in for a zero-collector setup that SigNoz/Langfuse already match.
